name: @thetis/tool-exec
description: Tools for the model: install, fork, remove, delete and configure packages, and spawn subagents in your own space. Running commands is @thetis/terminal.

tools.name: list_packages
tools.description: List the packages installed in your userspace: each one's name, version, type and description, the steps and tools it declares, its bench suites, and what it was forked from. The system prompt does not carry this list; call this when you need to know what is installed or which package provides a tool or step.

type.description: Only packages of this type, such as tool, loader, provider, skill or service

tools.name: install_package
tools.description: Install a package into your userspace from a directory path (relative to home) or a git URL. The package must have a package.json with a thetis field and be scoped @<you>/<name>. It becomes live on the next turn.

tools.name: uninstall_package
tools.description: Remove an installed package from your userspace by name. Its files stay. When it was a fork that replaced another package, that package comes back.

tools.name: fork_package
tools.description: Copy an installed package into packages/<as> under your home as @<you>/<as>, ready to edit and then install_package. Installing the fork replaces the original; uninstalling the fork puts the original back. Does not install.

name.description: The installed package to copy, such as @thetis/tools-plan

as.description: The directory name under packages/; default is the unscoped name

tools.name: delete_package
tools.description: Uninstall a package in your own scope and delete its directory under packages/ in your home. When it was a fork, the original comes back. Refuses @thetis/* packages.

tools.name: package_config
tools.description: Show what a package installed in your userspace is configured with: every key's state (set, missing or unset), which layer the value comes from and whether a fork inherits it, the value of a non-secret key, and the help of each declared key. A secret is shown as ••• and never its value.

tools.name: configure_package
tools.description: Set or unset one configuration key of an installed package in the person's own layer. Prefer asking the person to set a secret in the panel: a secret pasted into the conversation stays in the transcript. A key declared for the system is set by an admin in the panel, not here. The change is live on the next call. A string value may hold ${VAR} to read a variable from the environment; pass json: true to send a number, boolean, object or array. The reply names the key and its new state, never the value.

key.description: The key, as package_config lists it

value.description: The value to store; required unless unset is true

unset.description: Remove the key from the person's layer instead of setting it

json.description: Parse value as JSON before storing it

tools.name: spawn_subagent
tools.description: Start a subagent session in your userspace (same files and packages), send it a task, and return its final reply. The person watches the subagent work under its label. The first line of the result names it: [subagent <id> <label>]. Stopping your turn stops the subagent. A subagent may spawn subagents of its own.

label.description: A short name for the subagent, shown to the person, for example research.
